verdictRationale: The revision closes most registry-authority and lifecycle gaps, but the adapter activation model still has a circular enforcement problem. The spec says adapters are generated before doctor, disabled until doctor passes, and also extracted as active evidence before activation, which leaves implementation behavior ambiguous.

falsifiability.failureCondition: A generated adapter contains a registered command that is needed for activation, but the command is either enabled before doctor passes or never enabled after doctor passes.
falsifiability.observableSignal: In a fresh-install fixture, adapter extraction and doctor results disagree about whether the command is active and usable.
falsifiability.measurementMethod: Run fresh install against a fixture with one valid command registry entry, inspect the generated adapter before and after doctor, then run the extractor and assert the lockfile active set exactly matches the enabled adapter entries.
falsifiability.threshold: zero mismatch between active lifecycle records and enabled adapter entries

newIssueList.title: Adapter activation has a circular gate
newIssueList.description: The lifecycle says a capability moves to `generated` after adapter and inventory generation, then to `active` only after doctor passes. It also says adapter behavior remains disabled until the current doctor run passes, while adapter extractors must verify enabled entries map to registry records. This creates an ambiguous two-phase adapter contract: either adapters contain enabled behavior before doctor, violating the gate, or they contain disabled behavior and extractor evidence cannot prove the final active adapter state.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Define a two-pass adapter flow explicitly: render staged disabled adapters, run extractors and doctor against staged intent, then atomically render enabled adapters only for active capabilities and re-extract them before lockfile write.
newIssueList.lineRef: Capability Lifecycle; Adapter Extraction Gate; P2

newIssueList.title: Markdown active syntax remains underdefined
newIssueList.description: The spec now requires generated blocks and says active slash commands, rule includes, skill references, MCP references, and hook references may only appear inside them. It does not enumerate the exact Markdown patterns that count as reserved active syntax, especially for natural-language rule directives in `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. Without a concrete grammar or pattern table, extractor tests can miss behavior introduced through prose instructions.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Add a Markdown adapter grammar table listing every reserved active syntax pattern and state that arbitrary imperative rules outside generated blocks are either forbidden or ignored by generated harness adapters.

ledgerReview.rationale: The lifecycle enum and transition ordering are much clearer, but adapter enablement before versus after doctor still leaves active behavior timing ambiguous.
Per-type registries are now canonical, capabilities.yml is generated, and source digests provide an enforceable drift check.
Generated blocks and extractor mapping improve enforceability, but the exact Markdown active syntax and prose-rule boundary remain insufficiently specified.
The local override allowlist and denylist give validation code a concrete boundary with a hard failure mode.
Fresh install, managed upgrade, migration report, and migration apply now have distinct input conditions and failure policies.
Schema location, JSON Schema version, required files, validation command, and CI fixture expectations are now reproducible.
The lockfile is explicitly generated evidence, and doctor recomputes current state before drift comparison.
The allowed status enum and transition table give inventory, adapter, and lockfile behavior clear validation targets.

preserveList.summary: Per-type registries as canonical source with generated capabilities.yml and digest verification is the right authority model.
The install modes table correctly separates strict installs from read-only legacy migration reporting.
The lockfile trust boundary is now explicit and avoids treating stale generated evidence as proof of validity.
